p.src: Now, Jia Zheng had previously petitioned the throne to surrender the family residences and Prospect Garden to the state, but the court had declined to accept them. As no one lived there, he had no choice but to seal them up. Because the garden adjoined the quarters occupied by Lady You and Xichun, and its deserted expanses seemed far too vast, he punished Bao Yong by assigning him to guard the abandoned garden. At this time Jia Zheng was managing the household, and on Grandmother Jia's orders he gradually reduced the number of servants and economized in every possible way, yet still could not make ends meet. Fortunately, Grandmother Jia was fond of Xifeng. Although Lady Wang and the others did not much care for her, they acknowledged that she could still exert herself in managing the household and conducting its affairs, so its domestic business was once again entrusted to her. But ever since the confiscation, she had been unable to marshal resources as before and was constantly hard-pressed. Everyone in the various branches of the household, high and low alike, had grown accustomed to abundance. Now that their resources had dwindled by seven-tenths compared with former days, how could every need be met? Complaints inevitably continued without end. Xifeng dared not decline the responsibility and, though ill, devoted herself to pleasing Grandmother Jia. After some time, Jia She and Jia Zhen each reached the place of his assigned service. As they had money for their expenses, they settled down there for the time being and wrote home to say that they were living comfortably and that the family need not worry about them. Grandmother Jia was therefore reassured, while Lady Xing and Lady You also felt somewhat relieved.

p.src: One day, Shi Xiangyun returned to her maiden home after her wedding and came to pay her respects to Grandmother Jia. Grandmother Jia remarked on what a fine husband she had, and Shi Xiangyun told her that she was living peacefully there and asked the old lady not to worry. When Daiyu's death was mentioned, however, they all inevitably shed tears. Grandmother Jia then thought of Yingchun's sufferings and grew even more sorrowful. After consoling her for a while, Shi Xiangyun went round to greet everyone in the other households. When she had finished, she returned to Grandmother Jia's room to rest and said, “To think that a family like the Xues should be ruined and lose its members because of all the trouble Brother Xue caused! Although his execution has been stayed this year, I wonder whether his sentence can be commuted next year?” Grandmother Jia said, “You haven't heard yet. Yesterday Pan's wife died under suspicious circumstances, and it nearly caused another great commotion. Fortunately, Heaven has eyes: the maid she had brought with her confessed everything herself. Only then did Madam Xia cease making trouble and personally prevent an official examination of the body. Only then was your aunt able to send that living skeleton away. Just think—truly, the whole clan shares the same ill fortune! The Xue family has come to this. Your aunt now lives with Xue Ke, and because that boy has a conscience, he says that while his elder brother's case in prison remains unresolved, he will not marry. Your cousin Xiuyan also has a very hard time living with the elder lady. Miss Baoqin has not yet completed the mourning period for her father-in-law, so the Mei family has still not taken her as a bride. After the death of the second lady's uncle, Xifeng's brother proved good for nothing. Her second uncle is miserly too, and with official accounts left unsettled, he is also in financial difficulty. And since the Zhen family's property was confiscated, there has been no news of them at all.” Xiangyun asked, “Has Third Cousin sent any letters home since she left?” Grandmother Jia replied, “Since she married and went away, the second master has returned and told us that your Third Cousin is doing very well on the maritime frontier. But no letters have come. I worry about her day and night, though our own family has suffered one misfortune after another, leaving me unable to attend to it. And now no marriage proposal has been made for Fourth Cousin either. As for Huan, who has the time even to mention him? Our life now is harder than it was when you used to live here. I only pity your Cousin Baochai: since the day she married into this family, she has not enjoyed a single day of peace. Your Second Cousin is still as mad and addled as ever. What are we to do about it?” Xiangyun said, “I grew up here from childhood, so I know the temperaments of everyone in this household. Yet on this visit, they all seem completely changed. At first I thought they had grown distant because I had not visited for so long. But after thinking it over carefully, I realized that was not it at all. Whenever they see me, they plainly mean to be as merry with me as before, yet somehow, as soon as we begin talking, they grow sad. That is why I stayed only a little while with each of them before coming here to the old lady.”

p.src: Lady Jia said, “At my age, I can endure days like these, but how can you young people bear them? I have been trying to think of some way to let them enjoy one more lively day, but I simply cannot summon the energy.” Xiangyun said, “I have it! Isn’t Cousin Bao’s birthday the day after tomorrow? I shall stay an extra day, offer her my birthday greetings, and let everyone make merry together. What do you think, Grandmother?” Lady Jia said, “I have truly been so distracted by anger that I have lost my wits. Had you not mentioned it, I would have forgotten entirely. The day after tomorrow is indeed her birthday! Tomorrow I shall provide the money and arrange a birthday celebration for her. Before she was betrothed, we celebrated it properly several times; yet since she married into our family, we have not done so once. Baoyu used to be such a quick-witted, mischievous child, but now the family’s troubles have left him more silent than ever. Zhu’s widow has borne up well. Whether she has plenty or nothing, she remains just the same, living quietly with Lan. It cannot be easy for her.” Xiangyun said, “The others have not changed much, but Second Sister-in-law Lian alone looks completely different, and she is no longer quick in conversation. Tomorrow I shall try to draw them out and see how they respond. But though they may say nothing aloud, inwardly they will resent me and say that now I have—” At this point Xiangyun’s face suddenly flushed crimson. Understanding her meaning, Lady Jia said, “What is there to fear in that? You sisters were always accustomed to enjoying yourselves together. Talk and laugh as before, and do not harbor such reservations. Whether a person has wealth or lacks it, she ought to be able to enjoy prosperity and endure poverty alike. Your Cousin Bao was born broad-minded. When her family was flourishing, she was not the least bit proud; later, when misfortune overtook them, she remained perfectly composed. Now that she is in our household, when Baoyu treats her well, she remains settled as ever; and when for a time he treats her poorly, I see no sign that she frets over it. To my mind, that child is blessed with good fortune. Your Cousin Lin was exceedingly sensitive and suspicious, and that is why she ultimately did not live long. Feng has seen something of the world too. She ought not to have become a different person at the first touch of adversity. If she has so little understanding, then she is narrow-minded indeed. For Bao’s birthday the day after tomorrow, I shall provide money separately and give her a fine, lively celebration, so that she may enjoy herself for that one day.” Xiangyun assented, saying, “Grandmother is quite right. Let us invite all the other sisters as well, so that everyone may meet and talk together.” “Naturally, we must invite them,” said Lady Jia.

p.src: Her spirits rising, she presently said, “Tell Yuanyang to take out one hundred taels of silver and hand it over to the outer household, so that they may begin preparing two days’ food and wine tomorrow.” Yuanyang accepted the order and had an old serving-woman deliver the money outside. Nothing further occurred that night. The following day, word was sent out and someone was dispatched to fetch Yingchun. Aunt Xue and Baoqin were invited as well and asked to bring Xiangling with them. Aunt Li was invited too. Before half the day had passed, Li Wen and Li Qi had both arrived. Baochai knew nothing of the arrangements. When Lady Jia’s maid came to summon her, she said, “Aunt Xue has arrived and asks Second Mistress to come over.” Delighted, Baochai went over in the clothes she happened to be wearing, eager to see her mother. There she found her younger sister Baoqin and Xiangling, as well as Aunt Li and the others. She thought, “They must have heard that our family’s troubles have been settled and come to inquire after us.” She first greeted Aunt Li, then paid her respects to Lady Jia. After exchanging a few words with her mother, she greeted the Li sisters. From beside them Xiangyun said, “Ladies, please be seated and let us sisters offer our birthday greetings to Sister Bao.” Baochai stared blankly for a moment. Then it occurred to her, “Why, tomorrow is my birthday!” She said, “It is only proper that my sisters should come to see Grandmother, but if you say you have come for my birthday, I could never presume to accept it.” While she was still declining the honor, Baoyu arrived to pay his respects to Aunt Xue and Aunt Li. Hearing Baochai decline, Baoyu—who had long intended to celebrate her birthday but had not dared mention it to Lady Jia amid the utter turmoil in the household—was delighted to see Xiangyun and the others preparing to offer their congratulations. “Her birthday is not until tomorrow,” he said. “I was just about to tell Grandmother.” Xiangyun laughed. “What shameless nonsense! As if Grandmother needed you to tell her. Why do you suppose all these people have come? Grandmother invited them!” Baochai heard this but still did not quite believe it. Then she heard Lady Jia say to her mother, “Poor Bao has been a new bride for a whole year, yet one thing after another has happened in the family, and we have never once celebrated her birthday. Today I shall celebrate it for her. I have invited you, dear sister, and the other ladies so that we may all sit and talk together.” Aunt Xue said, “Your mind has only lately found some peace, Old Lady. This young thing has not yet had the chance to show you her devotion, yet instead she causes you further trouble.” Xiangyun said, “Grandmother’s dearest grandson is Second Brother, so how could she fail to cherish Second Sister-in-law as well? Besides, Sister Bao well deserves to have Grandmother celebrate her birthday.” Baochai lowered her head and said nothing. Baoyu thought, “I had assumed that Cousin Shi became a different person after she married, so I dared not approach her, and she paid no attention to me either.

p.src: Now, hearing her speak, she sounded just as she had before. Why, then, has ours grown even shyer since marrying into the family, so shy that she can scarcely utter a word?” While she was pondering this, a young maid came in and announced, “Second Young Mistress has returned.” Li Wan and Xifeng followed her in, and everyone exchanged greetings. Yingchun mentioned that her father-in-law was away and said, “I had meant to hurry over to see you, but my husband stopped me and would not let me come. He said your family was passing through an unlucky time and that I ought not let its ill fortune rub off on me. I could not prevail upon him, so I did not come, and I cried for two or three days straight.” “Why was he willing to let you return today?” asked Xifeng. Yingchun replied, “He said that Second Master of our family had inherited the title again, so it was all right to resume visiting and there was nothing to fear. That is why he let me come.” As she spoke, she began to weep again. Grandmother Jia said, “I was already distressed enough. Today I asked you all here to celebrate my grandson’s wife’s birthday, hoping that some talk and laughter might relieve my gloom. But now you bring up these vexing matters again and revive all my troubles.” Yingchun and the others no longer dared utter a word. Though Xifeng forced herself to make a few amusing remarks, she no longer had her former vivacity and could not make the company laugh. Grandmother Jia wanted Baochai to enjoy herself, so she deliberately teased Xifeng into talking. Xifeng understood Grandmother Jia’s intention and exerted herself to enliven the gathering. “The Old Lady seems rather happier today,” she said. Just look—how long has it been since all these people gathered in one place? Today everyone is here.” As she spoke, she turned and saw that her mother-in-law, Lady You, was not there; at once she fell silent. The words “everyone is here” also reminded Grandmother Jia of Lady Xing and the others, so she sent someone to invite them. When Lady Xing, Lady You, Xichun, and the others heard that the Old Lady had summoned them, they dared not refuse, though inwardly they were most unwilling. They reflected that the family fortunes were collapsing, yet the Old Lady perversely chose to celebrate Baochai’s birthday in high spirits—she was partial after all. Thus, even when they came, they looked listless and dispirited. When Grandmother Jia asked about Xiuyan, Lady Xing pretended that she was ill and could not come. Grandmother Jia understood: with Aunt Xue present, Xiuyan would feel somewhat awkward. She therefore said no more.

p.src: Presently, fruit and wine were set out. Grandmother Jia said, “Nothing is to be sent to the outer quarters. Today we womenfolk shall enjoy ourselves by ourselves.” Although Baoyu was now a married man, Grandmother Jia doted on him and still allowed him to mingle in the women’s quarters. He did not, however, share a table with Xiangyun, Baoqin, and the others; instead, a separate seat was arranged beside Grandmother Jia, and he offered wine in turn on Baochai’s behalf. Grandmother Jia said, “For now, sit down and let everyone drink. Toward evening you may go around and pay your respects. If you begin all those ceremonies now, everyone will fuss over propriety again and dampen my spirits. Then there will be no fun at all.” Baochai obeyed and sat down. Grandmother Jia then summoned a servant and said, “Today we may as well be thoroughly informal. Let each of us keep only one or two attendants. I shall have Yuanyang take Caiyun, Ying’er, Xiren, Ping’er, and the others into the back room, where they too may have a cup of wine.” Yuanyang and the others protested, “We have not yet kowtowed to Second Mistress. How could we go off and drink already?” Grandmother Jia said, “I have given my word for you. Go along now; come back when you are needed.” Yuanyang and the others withdrew. Only then did Grandmother Jia invite Aunt Xue and the others to drink. Seeing that none of them behaved as usual, she grew anxious and asked, “What in the world is wrong with all of you? You ought to be more cheerful.” Xiangyun said, “We are eating and drinking—what more would you have us do?” Xifeng said, “When they were younger, they were all high-spirited. Now they are too mindful of appearances to chatter freely, so the Old Lady finds the gathering quiet.”

p.src: Baoyu whispered to Grandmother Jia, “There is really nothing for anyone to talk about. If we keep talking, the conversation will only turn to unpleasant matters. Why not think of something and have them play a drinking game?” Grandmother Jia inclined her ear to listen, then smiled. “If we are to play a drinking game, we shall have to call Yuanyang back.” At this, without waiting to say another word, Baoyu left his seat and went into the back room to find Yuanyang. “The Old Lady wants to play a drinking game,” he said. “She is asking for you.” Yuanyang said, “Young Master, do let us enjoy a cup in peace. Why must you come and disturb us again?” “The Old Lady truly said that you must go,” Baoyu replied. “What has it to do with me?” Yuanyang had no choice. “You all go on drinking,” she said. “I shall be back soon.” She then went to Grandmother Jia. The Old Lady said, “There you are. Are we not going to play a drinking game?” Yuanyang replied, “Second Master Bao told me that the Old Lady had summoned me. How could I dare not come? What sort of drinking game would the Old Lady like to play?” Grandmother Jia said, “The literary games are dreadfully dull, and the boisterous ones will not do either. You must think of some novel amusement.” Yuanyang thought for a moment and said, “Aunt Xue is advanced in years now and will not care for anything taxing. Why not bring out the gaming tray and dice? Everyone can throw for the name of a song tune, and we shall wager cups of wine on the outcome.” “That will do,” said Grandmother Jia. She ordered someone to fetch a dice bowl and set it on the table. Yuanyang explained, “We shall throw four dice. Anyone who fails to throw a named combination must drink one cup. If a named combination appears, we shall then throw again to determine how many cups each person must drink.” Everyone said, “That is easy enough. We shall all follow your rules.” Yuanyang then arranged the order of play. Everyone made Yuanyang drink a cup, then began counting around from her; as it happened, Aunt Xue was the first to throw. u.src: Baoyu whispered to Grandmother Jia, “There is really nothing for anyone to talk about. If we keep talking, the conversation will only turn to unpleasant matters.
Why not think of something and have them play a drinking game?”
Grandmother Jia inclined her ear to listen, then smiled. “If we are to play a drinking game, we shall have to call Yuanyang back.”
At this, without waiting to say another word, Baoyu left his seat and went into the back room to find Yuanyang. “The Old Lady wants to play a drinking game,” he said. “She is asking for you.”

She then went to Grandmother Jia.

Grandmother Jia said, “The literary games are dreadfully dull, and the boisterous ones will not do either. You must think of some novel amusement.”

p.src: When she had finished, the dice bowl passed to Li Wen, who threw two fours and two twos. Yuanyang said, “That has a name too: ‘Liu and Ruan Enter Mount Tiantai.’” Li Wen promptly followed with, “Two Scholars Enter Peach-Blossom Spring.” Next came Li Wan, who said, “Having found Peach-Blossom Spring, one may safely flee the Qin.” Everyone took another sip of wine. The dice bowl came around to Grandmother Jia again, and she threw two twos and two threes. Grandmother Jia asked, “Does this mean I must drink?” Yuanyang replied, “It has a name. This is ‘River Swallows Leading Their Chicks.’ Everyone should drink a cup.” Xifeng said, “Chicks they may be, but quite a few have flown away.” Everyone cast her a glance, and Xifeng fell silent. Grandmother Jia said, “What shall I give, then? Let it be ‘A Duke Leads His Grandsons.’” Next was Li Qi, who said, “Idly I watch the children catching willow down.” Everyone praised the line. Baoyu was longing for a chance to speak, but the bowl would not come his way. Just as he was thinking this, it reached him; he threw one two, two threes, and one ace, then asked, “What is this?” Yuanyang laughed. “That is a ‘stinker.’ Drink a cup first and throw again.” Baoyu had no choice but to drink and throw again. This time he cast two threes and two fours. Yuanyang said, “There it is! This is called ‘Zhang Chang Paints His Wife’s Brows.’” Baoyu knew she was teasing him, and Baochai’s face flushed crimson as well. Xifeng did not quite understand and merely said, “Second Brother, hurry and give your line, and then let us see who comes next.” Baoyu knew the line was too awkward to utter and admitted defeat: “Just fine me. I have no next player either.” The bowl passed on and came to Li Wan, who gave it a throw. Yuanyang said, “What our First Mistress has thrown is ‘The Twelve Beauties of Jinling.’” Hearing this, Baoyu hurried to Li Wan’s side to look. Seeing the red and green dice evenly divided, he said, “This one is exceedingly pretty.” Suddenly remembering his dream of the Twelve Beauties, he withdrew blankly to his own seat and thought, “Those twelve beauties were said to be of Jinling; how is it that, old and young together, only these few of our household remain now?” He looked again at Xiangyun and Baochai. Though both were still there, Daiyu alone was gone; unable to restrain himself, he felt tears about to fall. Afraid that others might notice, he said he felt terribly hot and was going to take off some clothes; hanging up his tally, he left the banquet. Seeing Baoyu in this state, Shi Xiangyun supposed that he was unhappy because he had failed to throw a good combination and someone else had thrown it instead, and so had left. She also found the game dull and began to feel vexed. Then Li Wan said, “I shall give no line. Not everyone is present at the table, so you may as well fine me a cup.” Grandmother Jia said, “This game is not very lively either. We may as well call it off.

I shall give you ‘Autumn Fish Enter the Water-Caltrop Bed.’” Next to Yuanyang sat Xiangyun, who said, “White duckweed sung to its end—the autumn of the Chu River.” Everyone said, “That line fits perfectly.” Grandmother Jia said, “That ends the game. Let us drink a couple of cups and then eat.” She turned and saw that Baoyu had still not returned, so she asked, “Where has Baoyu gone? p.src: After they had waited awhile, Lady Wang sent someone to look for him. The young maid went to the bridal chamber and found Wu’er there trimming the candles. The maid asked, “Where has Second Master Bao gone?” Wu’er replied, “He is drinking over at the Old Lady’s.” The maid said, “I have just come from the Old Lady’s. Her Ladyship sent me here to look for him. If he were there, why would she send me here to find him?” Wu’er said, “Then I do not know. Go and look elsewhere.” At a loss, the young maid started back. Meeting Qiuwen, she asked, “Have you seen where Second Master went?” “I am looking for him too,” said Qiuwen. “The ladies are waiting for him before they eat. Where can he have gone at this hour? Hurry back and report to the Old Lady. Do not say he is away; say only that the wine has made him feel unwell, so he will not eat, and that he has lain down for a little while and will come later. Ask the ladies to begin their meal.” The young maid went back as instructed and told Zhenzhu, who reported the message to Grandmother Jia just as she had been told. Grandmother Jia said, “He never eats much anyway, so it does not matter if he misses the meal. Let him rest. Tell him he need not come back today, since his wife is here with us.” Zhenzhu then said to the young maid, “Did you hear that?” The maid assented. Unable to disclose the truth, she merely made a circuit elsewhere and then said that she had delivered the message. No one paid the matter any further attention. They finished their meal and then sat about chatting. But no more of this.

p.src: Now Baoyu, overcome with grief, came outside at a loss what to do, when he saw Xiren hurrying after him to ask what was wrong. “Nothing,” said Baoyu. “I only feel unbearably troubled at heart. While they are drinking, why don't the two of us go over to Cousin Zhen's wife's quarters and have a look around?” “But Cousin Zhen's wife is here,” said Xiren. “Whom would we be going to see?” “No one,” Baoyu replied. “I just want to see what the rooms where she is living now are like.” Xiren had no choice but to follow him, talking as they walked. When they reached Madam You's side of the compound, they came to another small gate standing half open, but Baoyu did not go in. They saw two old women who guarded the garden gate sitting on the threshold and chatting. “Is this little gate open?” Baoyu asked. “It is normally kept shut every day,” one of the women replied. But someone came out today and said that the Old Lady would need fruit from the garden, so it has been left open in readiness.” Baoyu slowly made his way over and, seeing that the side gate was indeed half open, walked inside. Xiren hurriedly caught hold of him. “There is no need to go in. The garden is unwholesome, and usually no one enters it. You might run into something.” Emboldened by the wine, Baoyu said, “I am not afraid of such things.” Xiren clung desperately to him and would not let him go. The old women came forward and said, “The garden is peaceful now. Ever since the Taoist captured the evil spirit that day, we have often gone alone to pick flowers and gather fruit. If Second Master wants to go, we will all accompany him. With so many people, what is there to fear?” Baoyu was delighted. Xiren could no longer insist on stopping him, so she had no choice but to follow.

p.src: Upon entering the garden, Baoyu saw desolation everywhere: the flowers and trees had withered, and the paint had long since peeled from several of the pavilions and halls. Only a grove of tall bamboo in the distance still looked luxuriant. Reflecting on this, Baoyu said, “Ever since I fell ill and left the garden to live at the rear, they have forbidden me to come here for several months, and in the blink of an eye it has become so desolate. Look—only those few green bamboo stems are still flourishing. Is that not Xiaoxiang Lodge?” “You have not been here for several months,” said Xiren, “and have even forgotten your directions. We were so absorbed in talking that we passed Happy Red Court without noticing.” Turning back and pointing with her hand, she said, “That is Xiaoxiang Lodge.” Baoyu looked in the direction of Xiren's hand. “Why, we have passed it!” he said. Let us go back and have a look.” “It is getting late,” said Xiren. “The Old Lady must be waiting to dine. We ought to go back.” Baoyu said nothing. Finding the old path, he went straight ahead.

p.src: Now, although Baoyu had been away from Grand View Garden for nearly a year, could he truly have forgotten its paths? It was only that Xiren feared the sight of Xiaoxiang Lodge would remind him of Daiyu and grieve him anew, so she tried to mislead him with her words. She knew that Baoyu meant only to go farther inside; but since it was growing late, she feared he might be assailed by some evil influence. Thus, when he asked her, she said that they had already passed it, hoping to keep him from going there. But she had not reckoned that Baoyu's heart was fixed solely upon Xiaoxiang Lodge. Seeing him hurry forward, Xiren had no choice but to catch up. She found Baoyu standing still as though he had seen or heard something and asked, “What are you listening to?” “Is someone living in Xiaoxiang Lodge after all?” asked Baoyu. “Probably no one,” Xiren replied. “I distinctly heard someone weeping inside,” said Baoyu. “How can there be no one?” “You are imagining it,” said Xiren. Whenever you used to come here, you would often hear Miss Lin grieving; that is why it still seems the same to you now.” Baoyu did not believe her and meant to go closer and listen. The old women caught up and said, “Second Master, please go back at once. It is already late. We still dare to walk about elsewhere, but the path here is secluded, and people say that since Miss Lin died, weeping has often been heard in this place. That is why no one dares come this way.” Baoyu and Xiren were both startled to hear this. “Then I was right,” said Baoyu. As he spoke, tears began to fall. “Sister Lin, Sister Lin,” he said, “I am the one who brought you to this, though everything should have been well! Do not blame me. It was our parents who decided everything; I was not faithless to you.” The more he spoke, the sharper his anguish grew, until he burst into loud sobs. Xiren was at her wits' end when Qiuwen appeared, hurrying over with several others. She said to Xiren, “How dare you bring Second Master to a place like this! The Old Lady and the ladies have sent people searching everywhere. Just now someone at the side gate said that you and Second Master had come here, frightening the Old Lady and the ladies out of their wits. They scolded me and ordered me to bring people after you. Why don't you hurry back?” Baoyu was still weeping bitterly. Ignoring his tears, Xiren and Qiuwen each took hold of him and led him away, wiping his eyes as they went and telling him how anxious the Old Lady was. Baoyu could do nothing else and had to return with them.

p.src: Xiren knew that the Old Lady was still uneasy, so she escorted Baoyu back to Grandmother Jia’s quarters. Everyone was still waiting there and had not yet dispersed. Grandmother Jia said, “Xiren, I have always known you to be sensible, and that was why I entrusted Baoyu to you. How could you take him into the Garden today? He has only just recovered. If he had encountered something and suffered another fit, what would we have done?” Xiren did not dare defend herself and could only bow her head in silence. Seeing how ill Baoyu looked, Baochai was deeply alarmed. Baoyu, however, was afraid that Xiren would be unfairly blamed, so he said, “What was there to fear in broad daylight? I had not strolled through the Garden for quite some time, so today, while the wine was still in me, I went for a walk. How could I possibly have encountered anything there?” Wang Xifeng had once suffered a terrible fright in the Garden, and at the mention of it every hair on her body stood on end. “Cousin Bao is far too daring,” she said. Xiangyun said, “It is not that he is daring; he is simply guileless. Who knows whether he went to meet the Hibiscus Goddess or to seek some immortal?” Baoyu heard her but made no reply. Only Lady Wang was so anxious that she could not utter a word. Grandmother Jia asked, “Were you frightened while you were in the Garden? We shall say no more about it this time, but whenever you wish to stroll there in future, you must take several more attendants with you. Otherwise, everyone would have gone home long ago. Go back now and sleep soundly tonight. Come again early tomorrow morning; I mean to make up for today and let you all enjoy yourselves for another whole day. Do not let some further trouble arise on his account.” At this, everyone took leave of Grandmother Jia and departed. Aunt Xue went to stay in Lady Wang’s quarters. Shi Xiangyun remained in Grandmother Jia’s apartments. Yingchun went to Xichun’s quarters. The others each returned to their own rooms. No more need be said of them. Baoyu alone returned to his room, sighing again and again. Baochai knew perfectly well what troubled him, but paid him no heed. Still, fearing that brooding might revive his old illness, she went into the inner room, summoned Xiren, and closely questioned her about everything that had happened to Baoyu in the Garden. How Xiren replied will be revealed in the next chapter.

Baoyu heard her but made no reply.
Only Lady Wang was so anxious that she could not utter a word.
Grandmother Jia asked, “Were you frightened while you were in the Garden?
We shall say no more about it this time, but whenever you wish to stroll there in future, you must take several more attendants with you.
Otherwise, everyone would have gone home long ago.
Go back now and sleep soundly tonight. Come again early tomorrow morning; I mean to make up for today and let you all enjoy yourselves for another whole day.
Do not let some further trouble arise on his account.”
At this, everyone took leave of Grandmother Jia and departed.
Aunt Xue went to stay in Lady Wang’s quarters.
Shi Xiangyun remained in Grandmother Jia’s apartments.
Yingchun went to Xichun’s quarters.
The others each returned to their own rooms.
No more need be said of them.
Baoyu alone returned to his room, sighing again and again.

Baochai knew perfectly well what troubled him, but paid him no heed. Still, fearing that brooding might revive his old illness, she went into the inner room, summoned Xiren, and closely questioned her about everything that had happened to Baoyu in the Garden.
How Xiren replied will be revealed in the next chapter.
